name: read.matrix
title: Whitespace-separated numbers, filled row by row. A header row becomes the names.

origin.description: Whitespace-separated numbers, filled row by row. A header row becomes the names.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: The series, matrix, or path this function accepts.

origin.details: Whitespace-separated numbers, filled row by row. A header row becomes the names.
origin.value: The same value tseries 0.10-63 returns for this case, written as one line.
origin.example:
tmp <- "/tmp/tseries-read-matrix.txt"
cat("1 2 3\n4 5 6\n", file = tmp)
m <- read.matrix(tmp)
cat("a b\n1.5 2.5\n3.5 4.5\n", file = tmp)
h <- read.matrix(tmp, header = TRUE)
paste(join(m), paste(colnames(h), collapse = ","), join(h), sep = "|")

translation.description: Whitespace-separated numbers, filled row by row. A header row becomes the names.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: The series, matrix, or path this function accepts.

translation.details: Whitespace-separated numbers, filled row by row. A header row becomes the names.
translation.value: The same value tseries 0.10-63 returns for this case, written as one line.
translation.example:
path = Path("/tmp/tseries-read-matrix.txt")
path.write_text("1 2 3\n4 5 6\n")
m = read_matrix(path)
path.write_text("a b\n1.5 2.5\n3.5 4.5\n")
h, names = read_matrix(path, header=True)
return join(np.ravel(m, order="F")) + "|" + ",".join(names) + "|" + join(np.ravel(h, order="F"))
